facts.text: Tobias, Nebraska, sprang to life in 1884 when the Burlington Railroad extended its tracks, turning the new station into a hub for local cattle and hog farmers.
The village earned its name from Tobias Castor, a pioneering settler who served as Saline County’s first clerk and later inspired the town’s official title.
Early residents of Tobias traced their roots to German, Czech, Irish, and English families, with German ancestry still dominating the community today.
Tobias experiences a hot‑summer humid continental climate, marked by sharp seasonal swings and moderate rainfall typical of the Great Plains.
